name: tfscript-vscode
description: Language support for tfscript, TinyFugue's macro language: diagnostics and command-name completion, plus syntax highlighting for .tf files.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Only reports diagnostics and completions for the open file; runs no workspace-authored code or config.

tfscript.entryFiles.markdownDescription: Files tf loads after `stdlib.tf`, in order — normally your tfrc. The server follows their `/load` and `/require` lines to learn which macros each file can see. Relative paths are relative to the workspace folder; `~` is your home directory. When empty: a `.tfrc`, `tfrc` or `tfrc.tf` at the folder root, else `~/.tfrc`, else `~/tfrc`.

tfscript.libraryPath.markdownDescription: tf's library directory (`TFLIBDIR`), the one holding `stdlib.tf`. Its files are read at runtime for hover docs and for `/require` targets. When empty: the `TFLIBDIR` environment variable.

tfscript.tfPath.markdownDescription: `TFPATH` as tf starts with it: directories searched for relative `/load` paths. As in tf, a non-empty `TFPATH` replaces the library directory as the fallback, so include it here if your scripts `/require` library files. When empty: the `TFPATH` environment variable.

tfscript.workingDirectory.markdownDescription: The directory tf runs in. Relative `/load` paths are tried here first — not beside the loading file. When empty: the workspace folder.

tfscript.diagnostics.unresolvedLoads.markdownDescription: Warn about a `/load` or `/require` on the load path whose file tf wouldn't find, listing where it would look.

tfscript.diagnostics.undefinedMacros.markdownDescription: Note `/name` calls to names defined nowhere on the load path and not tf commands. Off by default: macros created at runtime (`/eval /def`, hooks, files loaded another way) are invisible to it, though optional calls guarded by `ismacro` are skipped.

tfscript.format.splitStatements.markdownDescription: When formatting, put each `%;`-separated statement of a `/def`, `/bind`, `/hook` or `/trig` body on its own `%;\` line, and break after `/if (...)`, `/else`, `/then` and `/do`. Off: only re-indent the lines you already have.

tfscript.homeDirectory.markdownDescription: What `~` means in load paths (tf's `HOME`). Useful when tf runs somewhere else, such as WSL or a container. When empty: your home directory.

scripts.package: npm run build && npm test && vsce package -o tfscript-vscode.vsix
